stories.title: Islands Near Portugal Turn Off Lights to Protect Seabird Fledglings Every October – 30k Already Saved
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Every autumn on tiny Corvo island in the Azores, more than 400 residents turn off their lights for five nights in a row. It's not a power outage, it's on purpose: young seabirds get confused by artificial light and crash into buildings instead of finding their way to sea. Thanks to this simple community blackout, locals have rescued and released around 30,000 fledglings over the years. It's a beautiful example of a whole town pitching in for wildlife, no fancy technology required.
stories.why_good: A real, ongoing community conservation effort that has already saved tens of thousands of birds, with no political angle and a clear, happy outcome for the planet.

stories.title: Whale Festival Kicks Off on Amelia Island in Florida Celebrating the Return of the Right Whale
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: Every winter, endangered North Atlantic right whales swim down to the warm waters off Florida's Amelia Island to have their calves, and this week the town is throwing its annual festival to celebrate their return. It's been running since 2009, drawing families to watch for whale sightings and learn about the species. These whales are one of the rarest marine mammals on earth, so seeing them come back each year is a genuine bright spot for ocean conservation. The festival turns a conservation milestone into a joyful community event. It's a nice reminder that protecting wildlife and having fun aren't mutually exclusive.
stories.why_good: Celebrates the real, recurring return of an endangered species to its calving grounds, an actual event happening now, with no political or tragic framing.
